solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: By hot rod, shimmering silver accessory

indicators.note: something shimmering wavers and shifts, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A gleaming silver item is seen alongside a souped-up car.
explanation.walkthrough: A Dorothy bag is a small drawstring handbag, a term best known in Britain; 'shimmering' is the anagram signal, not a description of the silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dorothy bag is a drawstring handbag, a kind of fashion accessory carried on the wrist.

clue.text: Manage to perform surgery

definitions.meaning: to manage a machine or business is to run it
a surgeon cutting a patient open is working on them in theatre

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in carrying out an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both running something, like a machine or a firm, and a surgeon's work on a patient.

clue.text: Like Humpty-Dumpty, round and vacant?

parts.note: a round shape is a circle, the letter O
vacant means empty, void

explanation.surface: Humpty-Dumpty is described as round and empty-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: Humpty-Dumpty, of the nursery rhyme, is traditionally drawn as an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means egg-shaped, and the nursery-rhyme figure is pictured as a giant egg.

clue.text: Is shy changing suit? Tantrum results

indicators.note: letters that are changing take a new arrangement, so these two words are reshuffled

parts.note: to suit is to fit, as clothes fit a wearer

explanation.surface: A shy person forced to change clothes throws a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges ISSHY into HISSY; 'suit' looks like clothing but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal for a sudden, childish outburst of temper, a tantrum.

clue.text: Support old-fashioned soul about to start again

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person
a soul is a person, someone, so one

explanation.surface: Someone backs an old-fashioned person who is about to begin over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is used as it stands; the phrase, meaning returning to the very beginning, comes from old radio football commentary on a pitch divided into squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back to the starting position means having to begin a task over from scratch.

clue.text: Wizard, one in class

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, placed within the word for class

parts.note: a genus is a class or kind in biological classification
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A wizard is singled out as one in a class of pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard is informally a brilliant expert, someone of exceptional gifts.

clue.text: Happy clearing last away

indicators.note: the final letter of the woodland word is taken away

parts.note: a glade is a clearing in a wood

explanation.surface: Someone is happy that the last of something has been cleared away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clearing' reads as a verb but is the noun, an open space in a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words are synonyms, both describing a pleased and contented state.

clue.text: American soldier fed by a coarse Italian patriot

indicators.note: the soldier is fed, filled with the other words placed inside

parts.note: GI is the usual term for an American soldier
ribald means coarse, vulgar

explanation.surface: A US serviceman is given food by an uncouth Italian freedom-fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: A RIBALD goes inside G...I. A garibaldi is also a British currant biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi was the soldier who led the struggle for Italian unification in the 19th century.

clue.text: Bewilder leader of traders employed by a firm

indicators.note: the initial is taken on by, put inside, the other words

parts.note: sound means firm, solid, as in sound foundations

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trading boss is hired by a company, which bewilders everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective; T goes inside A SOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder and to amaze both describe leaving someone stunned with surprise.

clue.text: Protagonist in other opera

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the next two words

explanation.surface: The lead character appears in another opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The protagonist of a story is its central character, its leading man or woman.

clue.text: Other judge is poor

parts.note: a second one is another, as in a second opinion
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A further judge turns out to be no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of inferior quality, below the best, is described as poor.

clue.text: PM, extremely angry about note, makes appeal for help

parts.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister
D is a musical note

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A furious Prime Minister, writing about a note, makes a plea for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is loose here: it only sets the extremes of 'angry' right beside the note rather than around it. Theresa May was UK Prime Minister 2016-19.
explanation.definitionFit: The international radio distress call is a plea for urgent rescue.

clue.text: Extremely loyal butler worked round outskirts of Uxbridge

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the other two
something worked is shaped and reworked, so the letters of the servant word are rearranged
the outskirts of a place are its edges, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A butler made his way around the edge of Uxbridge, a west London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' looks like the butler doing his job but signals the anagram; 'round' then wraps it about the town's edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone staunchly faithful is described with this phrase; it also means a staunch Conservative.

clue.text: Local unmarried woman narrowly avoided collision

parts.note: local means nearby, near
Miss is the title of an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A single woman from the neighbourhood just escaped a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an incident where vehicles or aircraft came close to hitting each other but did not.

clue.text: Learns during actual practice session

indicators.note: one word comes during, in the middle of, the other

parts.note: actual means real
to learn of news is to hear it

explanation.surface: Someone picks things up at a real training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learns' looks like study but means finds out, as in hearing news.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-through of a play or concert before the performance is a practice.

clue.text: Hat, nothing more, for fashionable beach!

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: All you need at a stylish seaside spot is a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more' adds the nothing onto the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming area, originally a fashionable bathing beach like the one in Venice.

clue.text: Fool around thus, working with adults only just after

indicators.note: the fool word goes around the following pieces

parts.note: an ass is a fool
so means thus, in this way
a machine that is working is on
A was the old British film certificate for adults

explanation.surface: A clown messes about in an adults-only show.
explanation.walkthrough: A for adults comes from the old British film certificate; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediately when, the moment after something happens.

clue.text: Japanese drama about a biblical character

indicators.note: the drama word wraps about the single letter

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama

explanation.surface: A Japanese play tells the story of a Bible figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament patriarch built the ark to survive the Flood.

clue.text: Hammerstein perhaps dropping son at home with a wind instrument

indicators.note: dropping means letting go, so the letter for son is removed

parts.note: Oscar Hammerstein II was the lyricist of Rodgers and Hammerstein, an example of the name
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: The lyricist leaves his son at home with a woodwind.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammerstein is a definition by example, flagged by 'perhaps': his first name is the one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped flute, a simple wind instrument.

clue.text: Move on horseback, approaching hurdles

parts.note: a jockey riding in a race is said to be up
in jump racing the hurdles are called sticks

explanation.surface: A rider on a horse heads towards the jumps.
explanation.walkthrough: To up sticks is British slang for packing up and moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means leave one place and relocate to another.

clue.text: Bird that's seen in new trees planted in centre of Auckland

indicators.note: the rearranged trees are planted, set inside the middle letters
the centre of an eight-letter word is its two middle letters
new signals the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted among young trees planted in central Auckland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal on 'trees'; Auckland has eight letters, so its centre is the fourth and fifth.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon, a bird of prey known for hovering.

clue.text: Sound of boy in lift

indicators.note: the boy's name, said out loud, gives a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Philip is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy's voice is heard in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like an elevator but is a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or boost, something that gives a lift to spirits or sales.

clue.text: Devil-may-care Royalist

definitions.meaning: a supporter of King Charles I in the English Civil War

explanation.surface: A reckless supporter of the king.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means offhand or casual, and was also the name for Charles I's supporters in the Civil War.

clue.text: Work on model's face

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work of music
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone works on a model's face, like a make-up artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' looks like a noun but is the verb, to confront.
explanation.definitionFit: To face an opponent is to stand against and resist them.

clue.text: Steel structure only demolished after pressure applied

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the pressure letter

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

indicators.note: a demolished building is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A steel building is knocked down only once pressure is brought to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall steel lattice tower carrying power lines.

clue.text: Went on list prepared for Hollywood

indicators.note: words prepared are made ready in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone joined the list of people ready to head for the film capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinseltown is a nickname for Hollywood, mocking its showy glamour.

clue.text: Harmless piece of mischief in 17's vessel on lake

indicators.note: the vessel comes on, after, the lake letter

parts.note: l is short for lake on maps
clue 17's biblical character built the ark

explanation.surface: A prank is played in a biblical boat on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of fun or a prank done for amusement.

clue.text: Unlikely to add up if short

indicators.note: a word that is short lacks its final letter

parts.note: to tally is to add up, count

explanation.surface: Figures are unlikely to add up if the total falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'add up' also means to make sense, which fits the surface; here it is the count.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an unlikely, hard-to-believe one, so the adjective means improbable.

clue.text: In an enjoyable manner? Alas, plenty upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks if it's enjoyable, but sighs that plenty are distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes doing something agreeably, in a way that gives pleasure.
